content.text: The verifier's substantive review is fully affirming on every material term, and it confirms the no-redline/no-comment shape is correct. The only outstanding item is the deterministic check, which the verifier itself characterises as a phrasing artefact rather than a substantive gap. I will not manufacture a deviation or redline a compliant clause to satisfy a string-match check. I'll resubmit with the check resolution stated up front.

input.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
input.rationale:
COMPLIANT AT FALLBACK. No redline, no counterparty comment.

1. Deterministic check resolution. The "Customer convenience termination present" check fails on string-matching only: ¶4(a) grants the right to "Either Party" and never uses the word "Customer" in the operative sentence. The defined-term chain supplies the link — p0000 names The Associated Press as "the 'Customer'" and provides that "Each of Customer and Kubient may be referred to herein individually as a 'Party'." Customer is therefore a Party, and the ¶4(a) grant vests a no-cause termination right in us directly and on identical terms to the Vendor. The right is substantively present; only its label is generic. I have not redlined the clause to force the literal word "Customer" into ¶4(a), because the playbook directs that compliant clauses are not redlined and a cosmetic naming edit would achieve nothing while opening a settled provision.

2. Material terms.
(a) Customer convenience right — present, no-cause ("for any reason"), 90 days' written notice. Within the fallback's 60–90 day band.
(b) Lock-out — Initial Term is exactly one (1) year with 1-year auto-renewals. Not a term "longer than 12 months," so the walk-away test (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term) is not engaged.
(c) Early-termination cost — no fee or penalty. Kubient's entitlement to "all fees generated during the termination period" is revenue share actually earned across the 90-day notice window; it is consideration for services rendered, not an exit charge, and sits at or under the fallback's 3-months'-fees cap.
(d) Vendor convenience right — 90 days' notice, which meets rather than breaches the walk-away floor of "fewer than 90 days."

3. Noted, not escalated (minor sub-elements per playbook guidance). (i) 90 days' notice rather than the preferred 30. (ii) Vendor may exit at any time after the Initial Term rather than strictly at the end of a renewal term — the closest call against the fallback wording, but the right is exactly reciprocal on identical notice within a 1-year renewal cycle, so it benefits us equally and does not fail a material term. (iii) No pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, which is moot because §5 (p0023) is a pure revenue share under which Kubient collects from Advertisers and remits to Customer within seven days under sequential liability — we prepay nothing and have nothing to reclaim.

4. Contingency flag for the deal team (outside this rule's scope): if the commercial model moves from revenue share to any prepaid or subscription-fee basis, the absent refund mechanic becomes live and T4C should be re-run against the revised fee clause.
